Question:
In 1998, How many wins were made by team 'CAR' per game played? Who contributed the most goals? State the player ID.

Evidence:
year = 1998; wins per game played = DIVIDE(W, G); CAR refers to tmID; contributed the most goals refers to MAX(G);
answer: SELECT CAST(T1.W AS REAL) / T1.G, T2.playerID FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.tmID = 'CAR' AND T1.year = 1998 GROUP BY T1.W / T1.G, T2.playerID ORDER BY SUM(T2.G) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_1: I connect the team season record to its player scoring records by matching both team and year: `FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the joined records to team CAR in 1998: `FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.tmID = 'CAR' AND T1.year = 1998`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group by the wins-per-game expression and player so each player's goals can be totaled: `FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.tmID = 'CAR' AND T1.year = 1998 GROUP BY T1.W / T1.G, T2.playerID`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I select the wins per game with a REAL cast for division, along with each grouped player ID: `SELECT CAST(T1.W AS REAL) / T1.G, T2.playerID FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.tmID = 'CAR' AND T1.year = 1998 GROUP BY T1.W / T1.G, T2.playerID`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I order players by their summed goals in descending order and retain the top contributor: `SELECT CAST(T1.W AS REAL) / T1.G, T2.playerID FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.tmID = 'CAR' AND T1.year = 1998 GROUP BY T1.W / T1.G, T2.playerID ORDER BY SUM(T2.G) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Which college do most of the members go to?

Evidence:
college most members go refers to MAX(COUNT(major.college))
answer: SELECT T2.college FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id GROUP BY T2.major_id ORDER BY COUNT(T2.college) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.evidence: college most members go refers to MAX(COUNT(major.college))

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from the members whose college affiliations need to be counted: `FROM member AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join each member to their major so the associated college is available: `FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the joined rows by major to form the groups used for counting: `FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id GROUP BY T2.major_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I order those groups by their college counts in descending order so the most common one comes first: `FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id GROUP BY T2.major_id ORDER BY COUNT(T2.college) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I select the college from the top-ranked group and limit the result to one row: `SELECT T2.college FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id GROUP BY T2.major_id ORDER BY COUNT(T2.college) DESC LIMIT 1`.

Question:
Please list the various phone number types in the following order, from most to least common among businesses.
answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM PersonPhone AS T1 INNER JOIN PhoneNumberType AS T2 ON T1.PhoneNumberTypeID = T2.PhoneNumberTypeID GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC

metadata.question: Please list the various phone number types in the following order, from most to least common among businesses.

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with business phone records from `PersonPhone`, where each entry identifies its phone number type: `FROM PersonPhone AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `PhoneNumberType` to obtain the name associated with each type identifier: `FROM PersonPhone AS T1 INNER JOIN PhoneNumberType AS T2 ON T1.PhoneNumberTypeID = T2.PhoneNumberTypeID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the phone records by type name so each type can be counted: `FROM PersonPhone AS T1 INNER JOIN PhoneNumberType AS T2 ON T1.PhoneNumberTypeID = T2.PhoneNumberTypeID GROUP BY T2.Name`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I order those groups by their record counts in descending order, placing the most common types first: `FROM PersonPhone AS T1 INNER JOIN PhoneNumberType AS T2 ON T1.PhoneNumberTypeID = T2.PhoneNumberTypeID GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I project each phone number type name in that frequency order: `SELECT T2.Name FROM PersonPhone AS T1 INNER JOIN PhoneNumberType AS T2 ON T1.PhoneNumberTypeID = T2.PhoneNumberTypeID GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.Name) DESC`.

Question:
Among all the users who received the high number of compliments, what percent received the 'cute' type of compliment.

Evidence:
high number of compliments refers to number_of_compliments = 'High'; percentage = divide(count(user_id where compliment_type = 'cute'), count(user_id))*100%
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.compliment_type = 'cute' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.user_id) FROM Compliments AS T1 INNER JOIN Users_Compliments AS T2 ON T1.compliment_id = T2.compliment_id WHERE T2.number_of_compliments = 'High'

metadata.question: Among all the users who received the high number of compliments, what percent received the 'cute' type of compliment.

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `Compliments`, which identifies each compliment type: `FROM Compliments AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join the user-level compliment records through the shared compliment id: `FROM Compliments AS T1 INNER JOIN Users_Compliments AS T2 ON T1.compliment_id = T2.compliment_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the records to users whose number of compliments is classified as High: `FROM Compliments AS T1 INNER JOIN Users_Compliments AS T2 ON T1.compliment_id = T2.compliment_id WHERE T2.number_of_compliments = 'High'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I conditionally count the qualifying records whose compliment type is cute and cast that count to REAL before converting it toward a percentage: `SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.compliment_type = 'cute' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 FROM Compliments AS T1 INNER JOIN Users_Compliments AS T2 ON T1.compliment_id = T2.compliment_id WHERE T2.number_of_compliments = 'High'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I divide by the total number of user records in the High group to finish the percentage: `SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.compliment_type = 'cute' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.user_id) FROM Compliments AS T1 INNER JOIN Users_Compliments AS T2 ON T1.compliment_id = T2.compliment_id WHERE T2.number_of_compliments = 'High'`.

Question:
From laboratory examinations in 1991, what is the average hematoclit level that is lower than the normal range.

Evidence:
laboratory examinations in 1991 refers to Date like '1991%'; average hematoclit level = AVG(HCT); hematoclit level that is lower than the normal range refers to HCT < 29;
answer: SELECT AVG(T2.HCT) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.HCT < 29 AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Date) = '1991'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each patient to their laboratory examinations through the shared ID: `FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the laboratory records to hematocrit values below the normal range of 29: `FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.HCT < 29`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I then keep only examinations whose laboratory date falls in 1991: `FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.HCT < 29 AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Date) = '1991'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I calculate the average of the qualifying hematocrit values with AVG: `SELECT AVG(T2.HCT) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.HCT < 29 AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.Date) = '1991'`.
